title: The Merino Top Thrown Across a Lunch Table That Became Icebreaker
conflicts: Start-up capital: Unlimited (2005) says $250,000 from investors including Moon's parents; NZ Herald (2018) and Outside (2016) say $200,000; a sponsored NZ Herald piece and a Stuff headline mention $25,000 of Moon's own money. Story gives the two investor figures with attribution. First retail uptake: Unlimited says 20 of 60 targeted retailers in the first year; Outside says fourteen stores booked orders; story gives both. Farmer's surname Brakenridge (Unlimited) vs Brackenridge (Outside), and Pohuenui Island (Unlimited) vs Southern Alps (Outside); story follows Unlimited, which interviewed him.
notes: Episode as the slate described (the 1994 lunch and the 1995 founding), anchored on Rebecca Macfie's 2005 Unlimited feature (archived) and Moon's own archived biography. Funding changed from 'bootstrapped' to 'mixed': Moon mortgaged his house but also raised NZ$200,000-250,000 from family and his network. Outside's 2016 piece may be brand-assisted, so it is used only for Moon's recollections. A sponsored NZ Herald item is used only as a third support for the house loan. Quote stance: affirms.
